questions.q: She ___ to work by train every morning.
questions.why: With third-person singular (she/he/it) in the present simple, add -s to the verb.

questions.q: My brother ___ three languages fluently.
questions.why: A singular subject like 'my brother' takes the -s form in the present simple.

questions.q: There ___ a book and two pens on the table.
questions.why: In 'there is/are', the verb agrees with the first noun, here singular 'a book'.

questions.q: There ___ several reasons for the delay.
questions.why: Use 'there are' with a plural noun like 'several reasons'.

questions.q: The team ___ winning the championship this year.
questions.why: A collective noun acting as one unit takes a singular verb in American English.

questions.q: Everyone ___ happy with the final result.
questions.why: Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone' are grammatically singular and take 'is'.

questions.q: Neither of the answers ___ correct.
questions.why: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes a singular verb even before a plural noun.

questions.q: Either Tom or his friends ___ going to help.
questions.why: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here plural 'friends'.

questions.q: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.why: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb.

questions.q: The number of complaints ___ decreasing.
questions.why: 'The number of' refers to a single total and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: The box of chocolates ___ on the shelf.
questions.why: The subject is singular 'box'; the phrase 'of chocolates' does not change the verb.

questions.q: The students in my class ___ very motivated.
questions.why: The subject is plural 'students'; ignore the phrase 'in my class'.

questions.q: News about the elections ___ broadcast nightly.
questions.why: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Water ___ at one hundred degrees Celsius.
questions.why: Uncountable nouns like 'water' take a singular verb.

questions.q: Mathematics ___ my favorite subject.
questions.why: Subjects ending in -ics like 'mathematics' are singular.

questions.q: Each of the players ___ a number.
questions.why: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb regardless of the following plural noun.

questions.q: My friends ___ already arrived.
questions.why: A plural subject like 'my friends' takes 'have'.

questions.q: The dog ___ a long tail.
questions.why: Singular 'the dog' takes 'has' in the present simple.

questions.q: Somebody ___ left the lights on.
questions.why: 'Somebody' is an indefinite pronoun and is singular.

questions.q: The committee ___ divided over the proposal.
questions.why: A collective noun viewed as a single body takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Politics ___ never been my interest.
questions.why: 'Politics' as a field of study is treated as singular.

questions.q: All of the milk ___ gone bad.
questions.why: With an uncountable noun like 'milk', 'all of' takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Both of my parents ___ teachers.
questions.why: 'Both' is plural and takes a plural verb.

questions.q: The information you gave me ___ very helpful.
questions.why: 'Information' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'My sister ___ (work) at a hospital.'
questions.why: Third-person singular adds -s in the present simple.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'There ___ (be) two apples in the bowl.'
questions.why: Use 'are' because the noun 'apples' is plural.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Everybody ___ (need) a break sometimes.'
questions.why: 'Everybody' is singular, so the verb takes -s.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The list of items ___ (be) on your desk.'
questions.why: The subject is singular 'list'; ignore 'of items'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Neither answer ___ (seem) right to me.'
questions.why: 'Neither' takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'A number of people ___ (be) waiting outside.'
questions.why: 'A number of' takes a plural verb.
